title: Direct vs Regular Mutual Funds: What Changes Under SEBI's New Default Plan Focus?
description: Direct mutual fund plans offer lower costs because they do not include distributor commissions, leading to a higher Total Expense Ratio (TER) in regular plans.

faq.q: What is the Total Expense Ratio (TER)?
faq.a: The Total Expense Ratio (TER) is the annual percentage cost of operating a mutual fund, including fund management fees, administrative costs, and distributor commissions (in regular plans). It is deducted from the fund's assets before the NAV is declared.

faq.q: Is it always better to invest in direct plans?
faq.a: Generally, yes. Direct plans have a lower TER because they do not include distributor commissions, leading to higher net returns for the investor over the long term. They are ideal if you do not require or pay for advisory services.

faq.q: Can I switch my existing regular plan investments to direct plans?
faq.a: Yes, you can switch your existing regular plan units to direct plan units of the same scheme. This is typically treated as a redemption and re-investment, which may trigger capital gains tax based on your holding period.

faq.q: Will I lose my distributor's advice if I switch to a direct plan?
faq.a: If you switch to a direct plan, you will no longer be paying commissions to a distributor through the fund's TER. If you value advisory services, you might need to pay for them separately, either through a fee-only financial planner or by continuing with a regular plan.

faq.q: Does SEBI's focus mean regular plans will be phased out?
faq.a: SEBI's focus is on promoting transparency and investor choice, ensuring direct plans are readily available and understood. While direct plans are encouraged for their cost efficiency, regular plans will likely continue to exist for investors who prefer to invest through intermediaries and pay for their services.

faq.q: How can I find the TER for a specific mutual fund?
faq.a: You can find the TER for both direct and regular plans of any mutual fund scheme on the respective Asset Management Company's (AMC) website or on the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) website.

faq.q: Are there any upfront charges when investing in a direct plan?
faq.a: No, direct plans do not have upfront charges. The costs are embedded in the TER. However, some funds may have exit loads if you redeem your units before a specified period, which applies to both direct and regular plans.

fact_check.summary: The article accurately explains the differences between direct and regular mutual funds, SEBI's role in promoting direct plans, and the long-term impact of expense ratios. Most factual claims are verified by authoritative sources.

corrections.note: Corrected the claim regarding tax implications of switching between regular and direct mutual fund plans.

edits.why: Switching between regular and direct plans is always treated as a redemption and fresh investment for tax purposes, even within the same fund house, because they have different ISINs. There is no tax-neutral intra-scheme switch option.
